known_limits: The run-147 strand is a timing race and was not reproduced live. The regression's deterministic basis is the preserved run-147 hook stream plus real 2.1.223 composer captures, not a live strand.

The Governess independently misread the stranded composer as working in run 147. That is a separate defect, explicitly out of scope; this change makes the launcher fail before the Governess sees such a run.
The smoke's tmux stub has only enough fidelity to reach the kickoff seam. It is a cleanup and exit-code proof against the compiled binary, not a full tmux emulation.

tests/loop/bridge.test.ts has a pre-existing load-sensitive flake that is NOT introduced by this change, established by measurement rather than assertion. Failures always present as a ~5000 ms per-test timeout, never an assertion failure, and hit whichever of that file's subprocess tests happens to be running: 'bridge queues cross-agent messages for every Claude/Codex to OSS pair', 'bridge native fallback request is pending until Governess grants it', and 'get_task_result delivers only its exact queued utility handover' were each observed once. Mechanism: those tests spawn full `bun src/cli.ts __bridge-mcp` cold starts against bun's fixed 5 s per-test deadline, and cold start on this machine measures 57-3430 ms. Sampling: HEAD 14 runs / 3 failures, BASE 14 runs / 1 failure, with the decisive control being a time-matched base run that reproduced 'bridge native fallback request is pending until Governess grants it' at 5000.37 ms on the unmodified base commit. Cold-start medians, n=15 each, quiet: BASE 708 ms (p90 2037, max 3135) vs HEAD 827 ms (p90 2920, max 3430) - the distributions overlap heavily and the 119 ms median gap is far below the minimum effect detectable at that variance, so no regression is claimed and none is measurable. Flagged for the reviewer rather than tuned away, since the timeout belongs to an unrelated test file.
